title: The Longevity Genes in Founder Populations Project
official: Searching for Longevity Genes in the Historically Unique Ashkenazi Jewish Population
summary: We believe extreme longevity is due to specific genes which function to delay aging and prevent disease. The purpose of the research is to identify the genes/mutations associated with healthier aging; to understand the biological functions of these genes/mutations; and to develop therapies to replicate these preservative genetic activities in individuals who do not have the genetic profile for longevity.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Ashkenazi Jewish, age 95+,
* Offspring of person age 95+,
* Offspring of parents who died age 70 or younger.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Non-Ashkenazis
